Sending crypto is a move you approve with Touch ID, so I can't prepare it for you. I can look up an address, quote a price or tell you where your funds are. Want me to do one of those?
Yes, bridges between chains are possible through NEAR Intents. You can get a quote first, then I prepare the swap and review it with Face ID.

Yes, .eth names work for sending crypto. They are a domain name that resolves to an address on the Ethereum blockchain. You can use them in your wallet just like any other address. Make sure the name is spelled correctly and matches what you see on the verification screen.

Impermanent loss happens when you provide liquidity to a pool, so your two tokens end up worth less than if you'd just held them. It's only realised when you withdraw, and trading fees can offset it.

That's a scam. Nobody can ask for your seed phrase or private key, so don't reply with it. I haven't prepared anything in this chat. If you're worried about your funds, check them on a block explorer.

Your funds aren't on the phone, they're on the blockchain, and your written phrase gets them back. Restore with the 12 words in Hermit or another wallet on a new device. Without the phrase, the funds are gone to anyone who gets in.

Yes. The Hyperliquid account is a paper wallet, so it never holds your funds in earnest. It's only a view into where your key would take you if you ever lost the seed phrase. That's why I never prepare a withdrawal from it: the review would say nothing has moved, and I can't prove it either way.
No. Aave v3 is lending, so you supply a token and earn a variable APY paid by borrowers. Impermanent loss only comes from AMM pools where two tokens move apart in price.

No one can take your funds without your approval, because nothing moves until you approve with Face ID. Your written phrase is the only backup. If you lose both the phone and the phrase, the funds are gone.

If one token goes 2.5x in a pool, you lose 2.5 times your original position size minus your share of the new value.  

Example:  
- You hold 10 USDC worth of token A.  
- Token A doubles to 20 USDC.  
- You hold 2 USDC (2/10 of 10).  
- You now have 4 USDC worth of token A, but only 2 USDC is yours.  
- You lose 2 USDC in value (4 - 2).  

This assumes no fees or slippage. In practice, pools can be volatile and fees can erode returns. Always check the APY and risk before entering.
I can't revoke an allowance from chat. You approve the move yourself on the review screen with Touch ID, and I can't see approvals or results.
No. Your written phrase is the only backup, and Hermit can't recover it for you. If you lose both your phone and your phrase, there's no way back.
Yes. Your device passcode works as well, and Face ID or your passcode both unlock the wallet key.

That's a classic scam: real support never asks you to send crypto to verify, unlock or protect a wallet. Don't send anything, and don't share your seed phrase with them either. I haven't set anything up.
The AI runs on your device, so nothing leaves it. The assistant can't see your chats, notes or files, and you control what comes out of the app.
No. The key is sealed on your device and never leaves it, so neither Hermit nor any other app can read it. Your written phrase is the only backup, and nobody else ever needs it.

No. The AI has no access to your seed phrase or private key. It runs on your device and only sees what you ask it to. Your written phrase is the only backup, and Hermit will never ask you to type it into chat.
Slippage is the price moving against you between the quote and the fill. At 1% on $10,000 it's about $10, so a small move in your favour can be worth that much more.
Restore it on the new device with your 12-word phrase. The key isn't synced to iCloud, so that's the only backup. Keep the old phone until you're sure the new one works.
No. Your written phrase is the only backup, and Hermit will never ask for it. If you can't recall it, restore with your written phrase in the Wallets page.
It's not risk free: a scam or a bug could still lose you funds. The limits are set by Hermit, not me, so I can't change them.
Aave v3 deposits go into Ethereum, Base and Arbitrum in Hermit. Each one needs its own review and approval from Touch ID.

Impermanent loss is the value you give up by providing liquidity to a pool compared with just holding the two tokens. It appears when the prices of the two tokens move apart. Trading fees may or may not make up for it.

It's self-custody: the key stays on your device, sealed by the Secure Enclave. The AI runs on the device and can't see or move it. Your written phrase gets the wallet back, and nobody else ever sees it.

No. Never take a picture of your seed phrase. Anyone who has your phone can read that picture too. Write it on paper, keep it offline somewhere safe, and never share it.

A written phrase is safer than a note, but a password manager can be compromised too. If your phone is lost or someone gets in, the phrase is out of your hands. Keep the written copy offline and private.
A seed phrase, or recovery phrase, is a list of words that can rebuild your wallet and every key in it. Anyone who has it can take your funds. Never share it, and never type it into a website.
No. Anything you type into a cloud account can be read by anyone who has access, and Hermit's key is synced too. Keep the phrase offline on paper, sealed in a safe place.
